turns.content: Been a long day. Ten hours hauling 16-gauge spiral duct in this heat, and I'm beat. Got until Wednesday to tell Mateo if I'm in for duckpin bowling Friday, or I eat the forfeit fee. Then I open Instagram and see Toby, Julian, Sam all at Lake Chelan. They didn't even say anything in the group chat. Just a bunch of lake photos. Makes me wonder if they think I'm too blue-collar for that scene now.

Ten hours hauling spiral duct in that heat sounds exhausting. Seeing the lake photos afterward—without a word in the group chat—would sting, especially when you’re already worn out.

**The photos show they’re together, but they don’t tell you why you weren’t included.** It’s understandable that your mind goes to “too blue-collar,” but nothing you’ve described establishes that they look down on your work. This could be a smaller trip arranged separately; it could also be an exclusion worth addressing. You don’t have enough information yet to know which.

I’d keep the two decisions separate:
- **Duckpin:** Tell Mateo by Wednesday based on whether you want to bowl and expect to have the energy—not as a verdict on the lake trip. Set a reminder so the fee doesn’t make the decision for you.
- **Chelan:** Once you’ve cooled down and had some food and rest, ask whichever of the three you’re closest to privately: “Saw the Chelan photos. I felt left out finding out on Instagram—how did that trip come together?”

My recommendation: don’t decide what they think of you tonight. Recover from the shift, get a direct answer about the trip, and judge that answer alongside how they usually treat you.
Yeah, I get what you're saying about not having enough info. But it's not like they forgot to text. They posted photos. That's a choice.

Yes—posting the photos was a choice, and finding out that way can make being left out sting more. You weren’t part of the trip, and nobody mentioned it in the group chat. That’s a real reason to feel hurt.

But choosing to post isn’t evidence that they deliberately kept you out, or that it was about your job. Those are separate questions that the photos can’t answer.

You don’t have to prove a motive to bring it up: “Saw you guys were at Chelan. It hurt to find out through Instagram. How did the trip come together?”

I’d ask one of them privately before concluding what this says about your place in the group.
Alright. I'll ask Toby. But I'm not gonna pretend it's fine if he gives me some vague answer.

You don’t have to pretend it’s fine. Asking Toby directly gives him a chance to explain; it doesn’t commit you to accepting whatever he says.

If he’s vague, you can follow up once: “I’m still not clear on how it came together. Was there a reason I wasn’t invited?”

A vague answer wouldn’t establish that this was about your job, but it might leave your concern unresolved. You can say, “That doesn’t really clear it up for me. I felt left out, and I’d rather be direct about it.”

My recommendation: hear him out, ask for clarity if needed, then weigh his response against how he’s treated you over time—not just whether he gives the answer you hoped for.
Alright. I'll ask Toby. But I'm not gonna pretend it's fine if he gives me some vague answer.

That’s fair—you can hear Toby out without saying “all good” when it isn’t.

If his answer is vague, follow up once: “I’m still not clear—how did you guys decide who was going?” If that doesn’t clarify things, you can leave it at: “I still feel left out. I’m going to sit with this for a bit.”

An unclear answer leaves the question unresolved; it doesn’t establish that this was about your job. My recommendation is to ask directly, avoid getting pulled into an argument, and judge his response alongside the broader pattern of how he treats you.
Alright. I checked the group chat. There was a poll about Chelan. I just didn't see it. It was sent during my union exam week and got buried under a hundred study group notifications I muted.

Ah—that changes the picture. With your union exam and all those study notifications, it’s understandable how you missed the poll. The lake photos still stung, but there was a group-chat invitation you hadn’t seen, rather than the silent exclusion it looked like.

If you haven’t messaged Toby yet, you can reset the conversation: “Just found the Chelan poll—I completely missed it during exam week. Looks like you guys had a good time. I’d be keen for the next one.”

If you already asked why you weren’t included, a brief correction is enough: “Found the poll—my mistake, I missed it during exam week.”

My recommendation: drop the exclusion concern for this trip, set that Wednesday bowling reminder, and get some rest after that shift.
